answer: I would like to talk about a friend whose mind I have always found slightly intimidating. One of the most intelligent people I know is a close friend from university who studied physics, while I was doing business administration. We met because we lived in the same student hostel, and we have stayed close ever since, even though he now lives in Rajshahi. What sets him apart is not just how much he knows, but how quickly he grasps complicated ideas that leave the rest of us bewildered. He has this [[analytical]] mind that breaks any problem into neat, logical steps. I remember him explaining a statistics concept I had struggled with for weeks in about five minutes, and suddenly it made perfect sense. Yet he is never arrogant about it, which makes his intelligence all the more [[impressive]]. He is also [[intellectually curious]], always reading about subjects far outside his field, from history to economics. I think real intelligence is exactly this combination of sharpness and open-mindedness, rather than simply getting top marks. As for how I feel about him, talking to him is genuinely [[stimulating]], because he challenges your assumptions without ever making you feel small. I will admit that I sometimes feel a little slow beside him, but mostly I just feel grateful. Honestly, I always come away from our conversations having learned something, and that is rare. I suspect he will end up doing research abroad one day, and I will be very proud of him when he does.

followUps.q: Do you think intelligence is something people are born with?
followUps.answer: Partly, but I think curiosity and effort matter just as much. My friend was clearly gifted, but he also read constantly, so his intelligence was [[nurtured]] as much as it was inherited.

followUps.q: Do you often ask him for help?
followUps.answer: Now and then, mostly when I need to make sense of numbers at work. He is always happy to help, although he usually ends up teaching me far more than I actually asked for.

note: Added how we met (same hostel, my BBA vs his physics), a statistics example and a reflective close; upgraded plain mark 'curious' to 'intellectually curious'.
